title: Semantic fingerprint salting & cohort-TTL invalidation for embedding cache
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: High-traffic embedding/reranking endpoints see wasted model work on repeated or nearly-duplicate inputs (prefixes, minor edits) which increases per-token cost and p95 latency. Existing deterministic content-hashes cause both over- and under-deduplication: exact-match hashing misses semantically identical but textually different inputs; coarse fingerprinting sometimes produces collisions across tenants. Goal: implement a combined semantic+content fingerprint with per-cohort salting and a cohort-level TTL invalidation scheme to reduce false positives, improve hit rate for near-duplicates, and provide predictable invalidation windows for tenant-sensitive workloads.
motivation: Reduce token compute for high-volume customers by increasing cache hit rate for semantically-similar inputs while keeping false-positive reranks under control. Provide an operationally simple invalidation model (cohort TTLs and tombstones) so product teams can reason about freshness for mutable content (e.g., user profile text).
design_summary: 1) Build a two-part key: stable content-hash (sha256 of normalized text) + quantized semantic fingerprint (16B hash of 32-dim PQ code). 2) Add per-tenant cohort salt applied to the content-hash to prevent cross-tenant collisions and enable cohort-based TTL invalidation. 3) Store metadata: original input checksum, vector-approx-id, tenant id, created_at, ttl_ms. 4) On lookup: attempt exact content-salt match -> if miss, do approximate lookup using ANN index of quantized fingerprints with configurable distance threshold; if ANN hit above confidence threshold, use cached embedding. 5) Invalidation: cohort TTL eviction, explicit tombstones for user-initiated updates (via API call), and background scan to reclaim stale entries. 6) Operational knobs exposed in Console: cohort TTL, ANN radius, min-confidence, per-tenant dedupe toggle.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- ANN introduces false positives: mitigate via min-confidence and optional re-check using secondary model cheap-scan.
- Extra metadata increases cache size; we expect ~12% overhead for quantized codes and timestamps.
- Cohort TTL simplifies reasoning but may delay propagation of content edits if TTL is long; tombstones are used for urgent invalidation.
- Salting requires key namespace changes; must rollout with dual-read to avoid cold-start storms.
performance_targets:
- Improve effective cache hit rate by +18% for high-duplication 고객 workloads.
- Reduce P50 embedding latency by 12% and P95 by 8% for cached requests.
- Additional storage overhead <15% at 95th percentile.
- False-positive rerank rate <= 0.5% measured on evaluation prompt set.
implementation_tasks: Add semantic fingerprint encoder + quantization step in embedding pipeline
Schema change: extend cache metadata (content_salted_hash, semicode, tenant_cohort, ttl_ms, tombstone_flag)
Implement cohort salting management service (cohort assignments, rotate salt API)
ANN-backed fallback lookup with configurable radius and scoring
Dual-read rollout: read from old cache key and new combined key during migration
Tombstone API and background tombstone sweeper job
Console flags and per-tenant knobs for TTL and dedupe toggle
End-to-end tests and benchmark harness for hit-rate/latency evaluation
rollout_plan: Spike: prototype ANN lookup in staging against 5M synthetic items (team: Marco, Priya) - complete
Feature flag behind env var: enable_combined_key=false by default
Canary: enable per-tenant for 5 low-risk tenants for 48h and measure hit-rate/FPs
Dual-read period: 7 days to warm new keys (write both keys)
Switch read-path to prefer combined key once warmed and metrics stable
Gradual ramp to all tenants over 2 weeks with monitoring alerts
Post-rollout: remove dual-write after 30 days if no regressions
qa_and_testing: Unit tests for key generation and salt rotation
Integration test validating dual-read semantics and tombstone propagation
Perf benchmark: synthetic workload with 25% near-duplicate patterns to measure hit-rate and latency
A/B experiment with traffic split to measure user-visible rerank quality (human eval on sample subset)
Chaos test: simulate salt rotation and network partitions to validate no data loss
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end test shows >= +10% effective cache hit rate on production-like dataset
P50 embedding latency reduction >= 8% on cached traffic in canary tenants
Dedup false-positive rate < 0.5% on labeled eval prompts
Admin Console exposes per-tenant TTL and dedupe toggle and changes take effect within 5 minutes
Successful canary run with no customer-facing errors for 48h
